result.rationale: The finding is factually grounded: in the else-branches of updateEvent and deleteEvent (GoogleCalendarService), `externalCalendarId` is falsy (that's why the else branch runs), so `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match — the lookup is a no-op that always yields undefined. This is not merely cosmetic: the pre-diff code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` in that case, so the diff silently removes that fallback, changing behavior for callers that pass no externalCalendarId. The 'no-op' observation is verifiable directly from the diff lines.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` and `.deleteEvent`, the fallback path uses `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that case the predicate compares against `undefined/null`, so it will almost always return `undefined`, meaning `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` becomes `undefined` rather than selecting a meaningful destination calendar. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff (the find is effectively useless in the fallback branch).
